verdict: Dexcom grew revenue 11% to $1.3B and widened its margins sharply — operating profit rose 35% — though net income dipped slightly because last year's quarter included a large investment gain.

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: 64.3% of revenue, up from 60.5% a year ago

kpis.label: 2026 revenue guidance
kpis.note: Raised — implies 12–13% growth for the year

segments.name: United States
segments.note: Sales of Dexcom's continuous glucose monitors (CGMs — wearable sensors that track blood sugar for people with diabetes) in the U.S., mostly through distributors. Up 14%, the engine of the quarter, helped by the G7 15-day sensor rollout.

segments.name: International
segments.note: CGM sales outside the U.S., a mix of distributor and direct sales. Up 5%, slower than the U.S. this quarter.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the sensors, supporting customers and running the company. Up 13% YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing the next sensors and software — including the G7 15-day system and the Stelo app. Up 3% YoY.

otherDetail: Other income was $8M, net — mostly interest and investment income on Dexcom's cash and securities, less interest expense on its convertible notes. A year ago this line was $110M because it included a large gain on equity investments.
footerNote: Figures are rounded to the nearest $M from the release's one-decimal figures (revenue was $1,344.5M); $1M of rounding was absorbed in International revenue so the segments sum to the total shown.

takeaways.title: The U.S. is driving growth
takeaways.text: U.S. revenue rose 14% to $970M while international sales grew 5% to $375M. Dexcom again raised full-year guidance — revenue of $5.20–$5.25B — and authorized a new $1.0B share buyback.

takeaways.title: Each sensor is more profitable
takeaways.text: Gross margin widened from 60.5% to 64.3% — the cost of making sensors barely rose ($480M vs $478M) while sales grew 11%. Operating margin reached 24.3%, up from 20.1%.

takeaways.title: Profit dipped for a one-off reason
takeaways.text: Net income eased from $284M to $275M despite much stronger operations, because last year's quarter included about $110M of other income — mostly an investment gain — versus just $8M this year.

follow100Note: Per-$100 figures are rounded to cents; the chain lands within two cents of the $20.46 kept as profit.
